_about: Which areas ESRS E3 treats as (high) water stress, and how each criterion reads the WRI Aqueduct 4.0 baseline annual data (services/reference/aqueduct.py). A criterion no loaded dataset supports is named as not assessed, never assumed.

dataset.name: WRI Aqueduct 4.0 — current (baseline 1979-2019) annual water risk
dataset.citation: Kuzma, S. et al. 2023. Aqueduct 4.0: Updated decision-relevant global water risk indicators. Technical Note. WRI. doi.org/10.46830/writn.23.00061

2023.quote: Regions where the percentage of total water withdrawn is high (40-80%) or extremely high (greater than 80%) in the Aqueduct Water Risk Atlas tool of the World Resources Institute (WRI).
2023.ref: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772, Annex II (glossary), 'Area of high-water stress'

2026.quote: Global indicators (with associated datasets) and related thresholds to assess if an area is with water stress include: (a) baseline water stress – equal to or greater than ‘High’: 40–80 %; (b) water depletion – greater than ‘High’: 25–75 % (Seasonal); (c) baseline water depletion – equal to or greater than ‘High’: 50–75 %; and (d) WEI+ (Water Exploitation Index plus) – equal to or greater than 40 %.
2026.ref: ESRS E3 as amended by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1563, AR 2 for paras. 11, 13, 14 and 16(b)

criteria.not_assessed: no loaded dataset carries the seasonal water depletion indicator the text names
the EEA WEI+ (Water Exploitation Index plus) is not loaded

arid_low_water_use.reading: WRI's 'Arid and Low Water Use' class is its own category (its raw value is a code, not a withdrawal ratio): neither definition's percentage applies to it, so it is reported as its own class, not counted as water stress.

no_data.reading: No Aqueduct data for the basin: not classified.
